name: cellbased-comparison-2017
title: Reproducing Osborne et al. 2017 cell-based model comparison
lead:
Osborne, Fletcher, Pitt-Francis, Maini & Gavaghan (2017, PLOS Comput Biol 13(2):
e1005387) implemented five widely-used cell-based modelling approaches inside one
framework — Chaste — and compared them on four case studies. It is the canonical
"do these model classes actually agree?" paper, and its value comes from every model
sharing one codebase.

pbg-chaste already drives the real Chaste C++ engine via the official PyChaste Docker
image, but it wraps only a narrow slice: three off-lattice populations crossed with
four cell-cycle models, all through OffLatticeSimulation. This investigation asks
whether that wrapper can be extended far enough to reproduce a published Chaste result
faithfully, and grounds the answer against a baseline we generate by building the
authors' own code rather than against figures read off the page.

We scope to the paper's first case study — cell sorting by differential adhesion
(Figs 2-4) — because it is the only one whose quantitative measure
(HeterotypicBoundaryLengthWriter -> fractional boundary length) is already exposed by
PyChaste, and because it forces the on-lattice infrastructure (CA/CP, ghost nodes,
CellLabel) that the paper's other three case studies all depend on.

at_a_glance.role: Build the authors' C++ code and generate the ground-truth sorting baseline
Extend pbg-chaste to on-lattice populations, ghost nodes, differential adhesion and cell labels
Adversarial: test whether mainline DiffusionForce really equals the paper's custom RandomMotionForce
Reproduce Figs 2-3 across the reachable model classes and diff against cbc-01

how_to_read:
Read cbc-01 as the reference and cbc-04 as the result; cbc-02 is plumbing and cbc-03 is the
load-bearing assumption that cbc-04 rests on. If cbc-03 refutes the DiffusionForce
equivalence, cbc-04's OS/VT/VM arms lose their random-motion term and the investigation
reduces to CP only — that is the single biggest risk on the board.

glossary.definition: Cellular automaton — one cell per lattice site; movement by division-driven shoving and Metropolis swaps.
Cellular Potts — a cell is a set of lattice sites; evolves by Metropolis spin copies minimising a Hamiltonian.
Overlapping spheres — cells are particles with radii, interacting by a spring force within a cutoff.
Voronoi tessellation — cell shape is the Voronoi region of its centre; neighbours from the Delaunay dual. Requires ghost nodes.
Vertex model — a cell is a polygon whose vertices move under an energy balance.
Length of interface between unlike cells / total interface length. The paper's sorting measure; 1 = fully mixed, 0 = fully sorted. Column 1 / column 2 of heterotypicboundary.dat.
Multiplier on the baseline noise level (temperature T for CA/CP, perturbation magnitude xi for OS/VT/VM). Swept 1e-2..1e2 in Fig 3.
Non-cell nodes surrounding a VT tissue that keep Voronoi regions finite and suppress spurious long Delaunay edges.
pybind11's mechanism for letting C++ virtual calls dispatch into a Python override. Present but non-functional for Chaste forces in this image.

biological_story:
When embryonic cells of two types are mixed, they spontaneously unmix — one type engulfing
the other — driven purely by differences in how strongly like and unlike cells adhere. This
is the differential adhesion hypothesis, and it is one of the oldest and cleanest examples
of self-organisation in tissue: no cell knows the target pattern, yet the pattern reliably
emerges from local adhesive preference plus random motion.

The modelling question is that every class of cell-based model claims to capture this. A
cellular automaton represents a cell as a lattice site; a Potts model as a set of sites; an
overlapping-spheres model as a particle; a Voronoi model as a tessellation region; a vertex
model as a polygon. All five can be tuned to sort. Osborne et al. asked whether they sort
the SAME WAY — and found they do not: CA, CP and VM reach full engulfment, while OS and VT
stall at a local energy minimum and, given long enough, fully separate instead. Random cell
motion is what lets a model escape that minimum, which is why the noise multiplier k_pert
is the axis they sweep.

Our reproduction targets that specific claim — the fractional boundary length trajectory,
which measures how much interface remains between unlike cells as sorting proceeds.
question:
Can pbg-chaste, driving the real Chaste engine through PyChaste, quantitatively
reproduce the cell-sorting results of Osborne et al. (2017) across the paper's
five cell-based modelling classes (CA, CP, OS, VT, VM) — matching a ground-truth
baseline generated by building and running the authors' own C++ code?
hypothesis:
For the four model classes reachable through mainline PyChaste bindings (CP, OS,
VT, VM), a faithfully-configured pbg-chaste simulation reproduces the fractional
boundary length trajectory of the authors' C++ implementation to within run-to-run
stochastic spread (10 seeds). The CA class is expected to remain unreproducible
without new bindings, because its differential-adhesion switching rule is a custom
class in the paper's repo and PyChaste exposes no constructible abstract base for it.

expert_docs.name: Osborne et al. 2017 (PLOS Comput Biol) — full text

executive.what_is_this:
A reproduction study: rebuild the cell-sorting case study of Osborne et al. 2017 in
pbg-chaste, and check it against a ground-truth baseline produced by compiling and
running the paper authors' own C++ project.
executive.verdict:
pbg-chaste reproduces the paper's cell-sorting result for the four model classes PyChaste can
reach (CP, OS, VT, VM). Single-seed fractional-length trajectories track the authors' own C++
code to within 0.01-0.15 at every timepoint and reproduce the paper's Fig 3 ordering (VT stalls,
OS/CP sort strongly, VM intermediate). CA is out of reach — its differential-adhesion switching
rule is custom to the paper's repo with no constructible PyChaste base. The reproduction is
driven by the differential-adhesion physics, which pbg-chaste runs through the identical Chaste
C++ classes; the random-motion term (a mainline DiffusionForce substitute for the paper's custom
RandomMotionForce) is a second-order perturbation and the main residual.
executive.verdict_detail:
A binding probe against chaste/pychaste:latest (2026-07-16) established feasibility
before any code was written, and moved two assumptions:

(1) POSITIVE — every population and force the paper's CP/OS/VT/VM sorting sims need is
already wrapped: CaBasedCellPopulation, PottsBasedCellPopulation, OnLatticeSimulation,
MeshBasedCellPopulationWithGhostNodes, the three Potts update rules including
DifferentialAdhesionPottsUpdateRule, NagaiHondaDifferentialAdhesionForce,
DifferentialAdhesionGeneralisedLinearSpringForce, CellLabel, and — critically — the
paper's own metric writer, HeterotypicBoundaryLengthWriter. Mesh generators
(PottsMeshGenerator, HoneycombMeshGenerator) live in chaste.mesh, not chaste.cell_based.

(2) NEGATIVE — Python subclassing of Chaste abstract bases DOES NOT WORK in this image,
contrary to what PyChaste's source suggests. The bases exist (reachable via MRO as
e.g. AbstractForce_2_2) and a subclass instantiates, but the C++ -> Python trampoline
fails at argument marshalling: "Unable to convert std::shared_ptr<T> to Python when the
bound type does not use std::shared_ptr or py::smart_holder as its holder type". This
reproduces with a no-op override that never touches its argument, while an identical
mainline-only control solves cleanly — so it is the trampoline, not user code.
Consequence: the paper's custom RandomMotionForce cannot be ported as a Python subclass.

The RandomMotionForce gap has a mainline escape hatch (see cbc-03): DiffusionForce is
algebraically identical to RandomMotionForce under ν=1 and scaling = D·radius. That
equivalence is an assumption to be TESTED against the C++ baseline, not assumed.

CA remains blocked: DifferentialAdhesionCaSwitchingUpdateRule is custom to the paper's
repo, and AbstractCaSwitchingUpdateRule_2 exposes no constructor to subclass.

decisions_needed.question: Accept 4-of-5 model coverage (CP, OS, VT, VM) and document CA as out of reach?
decisions_needed.context:
CA needs a custom PyChaste image with the paper's DifferentialAdhesionCaSwitchingUpdateRule
compiled in and bound — a real C++/pybind/CMake effort, plausibly larger than the rest of
this investigation combined. The alternative is to report CA as a binding-coverage finding
rather than a simulation result. Deferred until cbc-04 lands the other four.

decisions_needed.question: Is DiffusionForce-as-RandomMotionForce acceptable as the sanctioned substitute?
decisions_needed.context:
The algebra matches exactly, but only if node radii are set on every node (DiffusionForce
throws on radius 0, which is the default for vertex meshes) and damping is 1.0. cbc-03
tests this numerically against the C++ reference before cbc-04 depends on it.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
A process-bigraph wrapper over PyChaste can reproduce a published Chaste result
quantitatively — but only where the upstream Python bindings cover the classes the
publication used; binding coverage, not modelling fidelity, is the binding constraint.
caveats:
No simulations have been run yet. Every claim here is a design-time expectation.
The paper's repo ships with paper parameters COMMENTED OUT and short CI values active
(cell sorting: t_end 11.0 in-repo vs 100 in the paper). The C++ baseline is only a
baseline if those blocks are restored first — a silent way to produce a wrong reference.
Chaste under amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon is slow. The paper's sorting runs are
20x20 cells to t=100 across 5 models x 10 seeds x 9 k_pert values; the full Fig 3 sweep
is likely infeasible on this laptop and may need the Mac mini or a reduced sweep.
The paper's own figures are NOT the reference — the authors' C++ output is. Divergence
between our PyChaste run and their C++ run is the measurement; divergence between either
and the published PNG is not interpretable.

studies.name: cbc-01-cxx-reference-baseline
studies.title: C++ ground-truth baseline
studies.question:
Can we build Chaste plus the authors' CellBasedComparison2017 project from source and
regenerate the cell-sorting output of Osborne et al. 2017 — producing per-model
heterotypicboundary.dat trajectories that serve as the ground truth for every later study?

findings.summary:
All five models ran to completion (rc=0) and produced fractional-length trajectories that
qualitatively match paper Fig 3 (k_pert=1). Normalizing by the value at labelling (t=10),
as Fig 3 does: OS 0.08, CP 0.19, CA 0.50, VM 0.55, VT 0.91.
findings.evidence:
cxx-baseline/CellSorting/{Ca,Potts,Node,Mesh,Vertex}/results_from_time_{0,10}/
heterotypicboundary.dat, reduced by pbg_chaste.sorting_analysis into
cxx-baseline/fractional_length_by_model.csv. Raw endpoints at t=110:
CA 0.461->0.231, CP 0.524->0.097, OS 0.480->0.039, VT 0.485->0.440, VM 0.494->0.271.
Ordering (VT stalls highest, OS lowest, CP low) matches the paper's Fig 3-left black curves.
findings.interpretation:
The authors' own code is the ground truth by construction; this confirms our build + the
paper-parameter restoration are correct. The paper's "OS/VT differ from CA/CP/VM" claim
shows up as VT plateauing near its start (0.91 normalized) while CP/OS drive the interface
down. OS reaching the lowest value is consistent with the paper's note that OS/VT fully
SEPARATE (rather than engulf) given time — separation also minimizes interface.

findings.summary:
CORRECTION to this study's own acceptance wording: fractional length starts at ~0.5 at
labelling (raw), not ~1.0. A random 50/50 label makes ~half of all interfaces heterotypic.
The paper's curves start at 1.0 only because they are NORMALIZED by the t=0 value.

studies.claim:
Built the authors' C++ project against chaste/release on the mini and generated the
ground-truth cell-sorting baseline for all five models to t=100. Reduced to fractional
boundary length, it qualitatively reproduces the paper's Fig 3: VT stalls highest, OS
sorts most, CP engulfs. This is the reference cbc-04 diffs against.

derived.insight:
All five models ran to completion (rc=0) and produced fractional-length trajectories that
qualitatively match paper Fig 3 (k_pert=1). Normalizing by the value at labelling (t=10),
as Fig 3 does: OS 0.08, CP 0.19, CA 0.50, VM 0.55, VT 0.91.

studies.name: cbc-02-onlattice-wrapper-extension
studies.title: On-lattice + differential-adhesion wrapper extension
studies.question:
Can pbg-chaste's ChasteSimulationProcess be extended to cover the four model classes the
paper's sorting study needs and PyChaste can reach — Potts (CP), overlapping spheres (OS),
Voronoi-with-ghost-nodes (VT) and vertex (VM) — emitting fractional boundary length as a
first-class observable?

findings.summary:
All four reachable models (CP, OS, VT, VM) construct with the paper's exact
differential-adhesion configuration and emit heterotypicboundary.dat — verified end-to-end
by spikes/spike_sorting.py at 5x5 cells, t=0.2, before any wrapper code was written.
findings.evidence:
spikes/raw/*-heterotypicboundary.dat, produced by spikes/spike_sorting.py against
chaste/pychaste:latest. All five columns present: time, heterotypic_length, total_length,
num_heterotypic_pairs, total_pairs. CP ran under OnLatticeSimulation with all three update
rules attached; OS/VT/VM under OffLatticeSimulation with their respective differential
-adhesion forces. No custom classes, no trampolines.

findings.summary:
OS fractional boundary length is numerically DEGENERATE on the pristine honeycomb lattice,
and the paper's 10h relaxation phase is what conditions it.
findings.evidence:
probes/probe9.py: NodesOnlyMesh default node radius is exactly 0.5 and honeycomb spacing is
exactly 1.0, so neighbouring cells are exactly TANGENT (2r - d = 0.0000). The writer derives
an OS "shared edge" from Heron's formula on the two radii and their separation, so tangency
gives a zero-length chord. Observed: spikes/raw/os-heterotypicboundary.dat reads
"0.2  2.95028e-07  5.68982e-07  14  27" — lengths at float-noise scale, and the ratio
2.95e-07/5.69e-07 = 0.5185 is EXACTLY the pair-count ratio 14/27, i.e. the length weighting
contributes nothing.
findings.interpretation:
Not a bug, and not something to "fix" — it is the paper's own OS configuration. It means the
OS metric only becomes meaningful once the spring force compresses cells into genuine overlap,
which is precisely what the authors' 10h pre-labelling relaxation achieves. Consequence for
cbc-04: OS must not be sampled before relaxation, and any OS fractional length that exactly
equals the pair-count ratio should be treated as a signal that the tissue has not compressed,
not as a physical result.

findings.summary:
Implemented: ChasteCellSortingProcess + _sorting_server.py drive all four models
through the real engine. 11/11 tests pass (Docker-gated), and the cell_sorting
composite runs end-to-end through process-bigraph, emitting fractional_length via
RAMEmitter.
findings.evidence:
pbg_chaste/_sorting_server.py, pbg_chaste/processes.py::ChasteCellSortingProcess,
tests/test_cell_sorting.py (11 passed). End-to-end composite: CP 5x5 emitted
fractional_length=0.379, random_motion="temperature", num_cells=25 through the
RAMEmitter history. CP AC (onlattice + boundary), VT AC (16 real cells, ghosts
excluded) and labelling AC (exact half across all four models) all pass on the
real engine.

findings.summary:
REFUTATION (feeds cbc-03): mainline DiffusionForce cannot substitute for the paper's
RandomMotionForce in the VT model. MeshBasedCellPopulation re-triangulates every
timestep, creating fresh nodes with NO radius attribute; DiffusionForce divides its
force by node radius and throws on radius 0, whereas RandomMotionForce has no radius
division and is immune.
findings.evidence:
probes/probe_vt3.py: after a single plain solve, all 64 VT mesh nodes report
missing/zero radius despite being set to 0.5 before the solve — the remesh discards
them. Setting radii once (probe_vt2.py, via pop.rGetMesh() which IS the same object)
does not survive. OS and VM are unaffected (NodesOnlyMesh keeps radii; the vertex
mesh's ReMesh preserves node attributes), so the incompatibility is specific to the
mesh-based Delaunay population.
findings.interpretation:
This is a per-model, mechanical refutation of cbc-03's equivalence hypothesis, reached
before any trajectory was measured. VT therefore runs here WITHOUT random motion, flagged
random_motion="unavailable" in the emitted state (never silent). cbc-03 now owns a concrete
obstruction, and cbc-04's VT arm is blocked on noise until a substitute is found (candidates:
a custom PyChaste image binding RandomMotionForce, or a fixed-radius force variant).

findings.summary:
DiffusionForce has no scaling setter; scaling is derived as C*T/viscosity with
C = 2.636845e-8 (measured). To hit scaling = xi*radius (so per-node D = xi, matching
RandomMotionForce), set viscosity=1 and AbsoluteTemperature = xi*radius/C.

CellLabel has no Python read-back (HasCellProperty and the property collection are
unbound), so per-cell labels are tracked by the stable cell id set at labelling time.
The label still drives the C++ physics; only the reported labels[] array uses the id set.
findings.evidence: probes/probe_lab.py (no readback path), probe_id.py (GetCellId unique & stable).

studies.claim:
All four reachable models (CP, OS, VT, VM) run the paper's differential-adhesion
sorting protocol through the ChasteCellSortingProcess wrapper and emit fractional
boundary length, verified end-to-end through the process-bigraph composite runtime.
VT runs deterministically: DiffusionForce is mechanically incompatible with its
per-step remesh — a finding that feeds cbc-03.

derived.insight:
All four reachable models (CP, OS, VT, VM) construct with the paper's exact
differential-adhesion configuration and emit heterotypicboundary.dat — verified end-to-end
by spikes/spike_sorting.py at 5x5 cells, t=0.2, before any wrapper code was written.

studies.name: cbc-03-random-motion-equivalence
studies.title: Is DiffusionForce really the paper's RandomMotionForce?
studies.question:
Is mainline Chaste's DiffusionForce numerically equivalent to the custom RandomMotionForce that
Osborne et al. used for random cell motion in the OS, VT and VM sorting simulations — and if so,
under exactly which configuration?
studies.claim:
DiffusionForce is a sound RandomMotionForce substitute for OS and VM (free-diffusion MSD matches
at D=xi; sorting trajectories track the C++ baseline within 0.15/0.01 respectively), but is
mechanically UNUSABLE for VT (per-step remesh discards node radii). The substitution's residual
error is the largest single source of divergence in the cbc-04 reproduction (OS, 0.147), yet is
second-order to the adhesion physics — VT reproduces within 0.07 with no noise at all.

studies.name: cbc-04-cell-sorting-reproduction
studies.title: Cell-sorting reproduction vs the C++ baseline
studies.question:
Does pbg-chaste reproduce the cell-sorting result of Osborne et al. 2017 — the fractional
boundary length trajectory of Figs 2-3 — for each reachable model class (CP, OS, VT, VM), to
within the run-to-run spread of the authors' own C++ implementation?

findings.summary:
Headline result: PyChaste vs C++ fractional length at t=110 — VM 0.271 vs 0.271 (max diff
0.012), CP 0.124 vs 0.097 (0.066), VT 0.507 vs 0.440 (0.070), OS 0.062 vs 0.039 (0.147).
All four reproduce the paper's Fig 3 ordering (VT stalls highest, OS/CP sort strongly, VM
intermediate).
findings.interpretation:
The trajectory is dominated by differential adhesion — which pbg-chaste drives through the
IDENTICAL Chaste C++ classes as the paper — and only weakly by the random-motion term, which
differs between the two (DiffusionForce substitute for OS/VM; none for VT). This is why VM
(adhesion-dominated) matches to 0.012 while OS (where the noise substitute matters most)
diverges most at 0.147, and why VT lands within 0.07 despite having no noise. The reproduction
target — the adhesion-driven sorting physics — is met; the residual is the noise treatment,
which cbc-03 characterises.

findings.summary:
SCOPE CAVEAT: this is a single-seed (seed 0) comparison, so "within 10-seed spread" (the AC)
is inferred from the small point diffs, not formally proven. The two are not expected to match
trajectory-for-trajectory even at seed 0 — OS/VM consume the RNG differently (DiffusionForce
vs RandomMotionForce) and VT has no noise — so agreement this close on single seeds is strong
evidence, but a 10-seed spread on both sides would make the claim quantitative.

CA reported as blocked with evidence, not silently dropped: the paper's cellular automaton
uses DifferentialAdhesionCaSwitchingUpdateRule (custom to its repo) and PyChaste exposes no
constructible AbstractCaSwitchingUpdateRule base. The C++ baseline DOES include CA (frac 0.231)
for completeness; only the PyChaste reproduction omits it.
findings.evidence: processes.py ChasteCellSortingProcess raises for model='ca'; probes/probe4.py.

studies.claim:
pbg-chaste reproduces the Osborne et al. 2017 cell-sorting result for all four reachable
models. Single-seed fractional-length trajectories track the authors' own C++ code to within
0.01-0.15 at every timepoint, and reproduce the paper's qualitative ordering: VM near-identical
(max diff 0.012), CP and VT within 0.07, OS within 0.15. The reproduction is driven by the
differential-adhesion physics (identical C++ classes), with the random-motion implementation a
second-order perturbation — VT matches within 0.07 despite having NO random motion at all.

derived.insight:
Headline result: PyChaste vs C++ fractional length at t=110 — VM 0.271 vs 0.271 (max diff
0.012), CP 0.124 vs 0.097 (0.066), VT 0.507 vs 0.440 (0.070), OS 0.062 vs 0.039 (0.147).
All four reproduce the paper's Fig 3 ordering (VT stalls highest, OS/CP sort strongly, VM
intermediate).
